guides.title: Tolls — France and Spain
bullets: France: pay at the booth by cash or card, or fit an electronic badge such as Bip&Go or Telepass.
France free-flow motorways (A13/A14, A79) have no barriers. Without a badge you must pay online within 72 hours.
Spain: AP- roads are usually tolled, A- roads are always free.
Spanish booths take cash, debit and credit cards including contactless.
A Via-T transponder or an international badge gives non-stop lanes across France, Spain and Portugal.
Much of the AP-7 coastal motorway is now toll-free, but some stretches and tunnels still charge.
Bip&Go À La Carte: € 10 activation, about € 10 shipping to Switzerland, € 2.10 per used month in France, € 2.50 in Spain and Portugal.

guides.title: Food — organic and clean eating
bullets: Prefer Demeter-certified, organic or biodynamic plant-based food.
France: Biocoop or La Vie Claire.
Spain: Veritas, the largest organic chain in Catalonia.
Avoid pork, which is everywhere in Spain: jamón, chorizo, fuet, lomo.
Avoid shellfish — shrimp, mussels, calamari and oysters are often hidden in paella.
Fin and scale fish are fine: dorada (gilt-head bream), lubina (sea bass), salmon.
Clean meats are fine: beef, chicken, lamb.

guides.title: Weather and packing
bullets: Tarragona in October: highs around 22 °C, lows around 13 °C.
October is historically the wettest month there — bring a rain jacket or compact umbrella.
Layers: t-shirts, light sweaters, cardigans.
A light to medium jacket or windbreaker for the evenings.
Comfortable walking shoes for sightseeing and camp.
Swimwear — the beach resort can still be usable.
Sun protection: sunglasses, hat, sunscreen.
A small daypack for outings, reusable water bottles, chargers, toiletries and medication.
